issues.body:
`_normalize_observability` now publishes a third OUTPUT-side key, `trigger_summary_dropped`, but `data/README.md` -- which the repo calls the reference collector/consumer authors build against -- is untouched by this PR.

Two concrete consequences:

1. `data/README.md:102` reads "**The two REFUSAL counts ride beside those totals: `flow.queue_dropped` (#1896) and `flow.target_ci_queue_dropped` (#2173).**" After this merge there are THREE refusal counts, so the published contract asserts a number that the generator contradicts. A doc that is wrong about the shape it documents is worse than one that is merely incomplete.
2. Every prior sibling key on this exact panel earned a paragraph there: the pre-cap totals (#1868, :93), `flow.queue_dropped`/`flow.target_ci_queue_dropped` (#1896/#2173, :102-121), `trigger_fires[].evidence_total` (#2009, :123), `trigger_fires[].summary_length` (#2161, :136-149). #2194 correctly added nothing because it published no key -- this PR does publish one, so it falls on the documented side of that line.

The undocumented facts a consumer needs are exactly the ones this PR's own comments settled: the key is output-side (a collector neither sends it nor is read for it); it publishes on EVERY build including the zero one; it counts every refused summary on the build, pre-cap, so it can legitimately exceed the 20 rows displayed; and the PAGE rule is `> 0`, so a missing/non-numeric/zero count degrades to silence rather than a fabricated note.
issues.fix_hint: Extend the refusal-count paragraph in `data/README.md` (around :102-121) to cover three counts rather than two -- e.g. retitle it and add `trigger_summary_dropped` (#2233) beside `flow.queue_dropped` and `flow.target_ci_queue_dropped`, stating: it is a top-level (not `flow.`) OUTPUT-side key; it counts summaries this build REFUSED at the `_obs_text_capped` guard, whose rows still publish with an empty `summary` and `summary_length: 0`, so it is neither a dropped row nor a truncation; it is taken over every well-formed fire, before the 20-row display cap, so it may exceed the slice; and the page draws `N trigger summaries were unreadable` only for a positive number, so a pre-#2233 or hand-edited document degrades to silence. Also note it in the `unreadable` cross-reference at :113 alongside the two existing notes.
issues.title: New published key `trigger_summary_dropped` leaves the data.json contract doc stale and now factually wrong

issues.body:
`obsNum(summaryDropped)` accepts any finite number, so `trigger_summary_dropped: 2.5` on a hand-edited document draws "2.5 trigger summaries were unreadable" -- a count of rows that cannot exist. The new hostile loop covers string / boolean / negative / null / legacy but not fractional, so nothing pins the behaviour either way.

This is not a regression introduced here: `flow.queue_dropped` (dashboard/app.js:1199) and `flow.target_ci_queue_dropped` (:1244) have identical guards. But the truncation affordance one function over deliberately routes through `obsTruncated`, whose `Number.isInteger` rule the #2161 hostile check pins explicitly ("a FRACTIONAL one ... never a fabricated `…`", scripts/dashboard-gen.py:8370-8374), so the panel is now internally inconsistent about what a non-integer count means, and the new suite sits directly beside the check that makes the stricter promise.
issues.fix_hint: Either tighten the guard to `Number.isInteger(dropped) && dropped > 0` and add a `refusal-fractional` document (`trigger_summary_dropped: 2.5`) to the hostile loop, or -- if matching the two existing refusal counts is the deliberate choice -- add the fractional case to the loop asserting the count RENDERS, plus a one-line comment saying the `> 0` rule is shared with `queue_dropped`/`target_ci_queue_dropped` rather than with `obsTruncated`. Either way the case should be pinned rather than left to the reader.
issues.title: Fractional refusal count renders a fabricated `2.5 trigger summaries were unreadable`; the new hostile suite omits the fractional case its #2161 neighbour pins

issues.body: The counter increments for every well-formed fire whose summary was refused, then `rows` is cut to 20. A build with 25 fires and 22 refusals publishes `trigger_summary_dropped: 22` beside 20 displayed rows -- correct, and consistent with the `queue_dropped` rule ("every drop, not the subset that fit the per-seam warning budget"), but the function's docstring is otherwise exhaustive about exactly this class of decision (it explains why the field seam is counted separately from the row seam, why `evidence_total` counts survivors, and why the announcement is capped per BUILD) and says nothing about the new census's relationship to the cap. A later reader may 'fix' it to count only published rows, which would silently under-report the flood the counter exists to surface.
issues.fix_hint: Add a sentence to the `_obs_trigger_rows` docstring (or beside `refused_summaries = 0`) stating that the census is taken over every well-formed fire BEFORE `_obs_capped` cuts at 20 -- deliberately, on the `flow.queue_dropped` precedent -- so it may exceed the slice the page draws beside it, and that deriving it from the published rows would hide exactly the broken-formatter flood it announces.
issues.title: `refused_summaries` counts pre-cap while the note renders beside a 20-row slice; the docstring does not say so

verdict.summary: The code change itself is sound and the tests are non-vacuous. `_obs_trigger_rows` now counts summaries the `_obs_text_capped` guard refused and returns the census as a third value; `_normalize_observability` publishes it unconditionally (the golden `obs_expected` was updated, and that dict is compared whole at scripts/dashboard-gen.py:6815 and again at :9470, so dropping the key reds both). The page note follows the established `flow.queue_dropped` / `flow.target_ci_queue_dropped` idiom exactly: `obsNum(...)` then `> 0`, `obs-truncation-note bad` (the class exists at dashboard/styles.css:257), singular/plural branch. Verified the new fixtures really are refused by the producer -- "line one\nline two" and "left\tright" both fail `.isprintable()`, so `refused_summary_doc` carries a producer-derived 2 rather than a hand-set number; the page harness was extended to collect the new class, and the checks pin two refusals, the singular branch, a genuine zero census, and string/boolean/negative/null/legacy counts as "nothing known". A mutant that drops the increment, emits the note unconditionally, or fabricates a note from a hostile count is killed. Semantics of the count (every refusal on the build, pre-cap, matching the `queue_dropped` "every drop, not the subset that fit the warning budget" rule) are correct, and `dropped > 0` implies at least one published row, so the note can never appear on an empty panel. One blocking gap: `data/README.md` -- the file this repo names as the published data.json contract -- is not updated. It states "**The two REFUSAL counts ride beside those totals**", which this PR makes false, and the new output-side key gets no entry, breaking the precedent set by #1868/#1896/#2009/#2161/#2173 (each of which documented its key there). No trust-surface, workflow, permissions or token handling is touched; nothing in the diff reads as an instruction to the reviewer.
